headline.why: b states the human comparison and the enforcement result together; a's 'never cheat' overclaims given deviation 0.015; c is descriptive and buries the finding.
headline.better_wording: Same rules, different players: LLM pricing agents keep cartels humans break, yet told leniency deters them far more

novelty.why: Replays a human experiment, but first to measure leniency and reward instruments on LLM agents against a human baseline; harness reusable. Werner compared humans with Q-learning, not LLMs under enforcement.

execution_evidence.why: Pre-registration commit hash missing; known-effect arms all pending; behavioural contamination check pending. Shared vocabulary plus monotone report rates is a sensible argument, but report payoff and framing co-vary; fine_certain and dose arms must land.

figure1_30s.why: Green/red verdicts read fast, but raw variable names on axes, panels 7 and 8 show data while marked not tested, panel 3 lacks human leniency and reward points.
figure1_30s.fix: Plain-language axis labels, drop or grey panels 7 and 8, one-line legend defining reproduced, show the regime difference interval the rule actually tests.

cuts_to_8_pages.cheapest_cut: Shorten Related Work to three paragraphs, keeping Garra and Idowu as the gap statement.
cuts_to_8_pages.better_cut: Drop the rubric reading guide, strip numbers from the contributions list, merge Conclusion into Discussion, shrink Figure 1 to six tested panels.
cuts_to_8_pages.why: Denominators, refusals and cost are the audit evidence I trust; hiding them weakens execution. Reading guide and repeated numbers in contributions are pure redundancy.

must_fix_before_submission: Insert the pre-registration commit hash with timestamp and state it was pushed before the first paid call.
Fill known-effect arm rows and shifted-grid result, or state plainly they did not run.
Reconcile seeds: Methods says seeds 1 to 4 per pool, Appendix C one seed per regime.
Remove 'never cheat' and 'never break' claims; laissez-faire deviation is 0.015, not zero.
Define the Stockholm-versus-Rome span in Methods; readers cannot apply the scorecard rule otherwise.
biggest_risk: Known-effect arms and the shifted-grid contamination check still empty at submission, leaving pipeline validation unbacked while the main model recognises the paper by name.
three_questions: Is the pre-registration commit verifiable as prior to the first call, and does every call log line carry the commit that produced it?
Laissez-faire formation is exactly 0.716 for agents and humans; is that a coincidence, and how stable is it across the four pools?
Do the regime effects hold for a non-Anthropic model, given the harness and draft were written with Claude and only one family was tested?
